prompt: What is the area of the shaded triangle?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The vertices are $(0,0)$, $(2,4)$ and $(5,1)$. Using the shoelace formula, area $=\frac12|2\cdot1-4\cdot5|=\frac12\times18=9$.

Check: enclose the triangle in the rectangle $[0,5]\times[0,4]$ of area 20 and subtract the three right triangles: $\frac12\cdot2\cdot4=4$, $\frac12\cdot3\cdot3=4.5$, $\frac12\cdot5\cdot1=2.5$, giving $20-11=9$.

**Answer: 9 square units**

prompt: What is the product of the smallest two-digit triangular number and the largest two-digit prime number?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Triangular numbers are $1,3,6,10,\ldots$ so the smallest two-digit one is $10$. The largest two-digit prime is $97$. $10\times97=970$.

**Answer: 970**

prompt: Each of five pupils has a different number of pens in their pencil cases. The mean is 6.4 pens. What is the highest possible number of pens in a pencil case?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The total is $5\times6.4=32$. To make one case as large as possible the other four must be as small as possible and different: $1,2,3,4$, which total $10$ (each pupil has at least one pen). The largest is $32-10=22$.

**Answer: 22 pens**

reviewNote: Official answer 22 assumes every pencil case contains at least one pen; if an empty case (0 pens) were allowed the answer would be 26.

prompt: In one week Sonja works for $17\frac12$ hours at £8.40 an hour and then 8 hours at £9.00 per hour. 25% of this gross wage is deducted for tax, etc. What is left per week?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$17.5\times8.40=147$ and $8\times9=72$, so the gross wage is $£219$. 75% is left: $0.75\times219=164.25$.

**Answer: £164.25**

prompt: What is the size of the smallest angle in a triangle whose angles are $3x^\circ$, $4x^\circ$ and $5x^\circ$?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$3x+4x+5x=180$ gives $x=15$. The smallest angle is $3x=45$ degrees.

**Answer: 45 degrees**

prompt: An odd three-digit number less than 200 has digit product 4. What is the number?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The first digit is 1, so the other two digits multiply to 4: $(1,4),(4,1),(2,2)$. The number must be odd, which leaves $141$ ($114$ and $122$ are even).

**Answer: 141**

prompt: On a map with scale 1:50 000, the path Martha is going to walk is 4 cm long. She walks at 4 km per hour. In minutes, how long will it take her?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
4 cm on the map is $4\times50\,000=200\,000$ cm $=2$ km. At 4 km/h this takes half an hour, i.e. 30 minutes.

**Answer: 30 minutes**

prompt: The diagram shows the pattern of square slabs that form a patio. The area of the patio is 5.67 square metres. What is the perimeter?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
There are 7 slabs, so one slab has area $5.67/7=0.81$ m$^2$ and side $0.9$ m. The perimeter of the pattern equals that of its $3\times3$ bounding square, i.e. $12$ slab sides: $12\times0.9=10.8$ m.

**Answer: 10.8 metres**

prompt: A mathematical grandmother allows her six grandchildren equal shares of her dog-walking for 2016. Art does all his share first, starting on 1 January. What is the date when Bert takes over from Art?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
2016 is a leap year with 366 days, so each share is $366/6=61$ days. Art's 61 days: January (31) + February (29) = 60 days, plus 1 March. Bert starts on 2 March.

**Answer: 2nd March**

prompt: Amid is planning to take part in a long-distance cycle race. His training route is 49 km long, as shown. He cycles at an average speed of 30 km per hour along the flat, 24 km per hour uphill and 40 km per hour downhill. How many minutes does he take to cover one circuit?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Uphill: $6/24$ h $=15$ min. Downhill: $8/40$ h $=12$ min. Flat: $10+25=35$ km at 30 km/h $=70$ min. Total $15+12+70=97$ minutes.

**Answer: 97 minutes**

prompt: A train left the station at 10:16, twenty-three minutes late. The driver was not able to make up any of the time and so the train took the same length of time as usual to reach the next station, that is, 89 minutes. At what time should the train have arrived if it was on time?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
It should have left at $10:16-23\text{ min}=09:53$. Adding the 89-minute journey: $09:53+1\text{ h }29\text{ min}=11:22$.

**Answer: 11:22**

prompt: Let $t$ be the number of edges of a triangle. Let $q$ be the number of edges of a quadrilateral. Let $p$ be the number of edges of a pentagon. Let $d$ be the number of edges of a decagon. Let $e$ be the number of even prime numbers. Let $s$ be the smallest prime number. Calculate $d^2(tqp+e)+s$.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$t=3$, $q=4$, $p=5$, $d=10$, $e=1$ (only 2 is an even prime) and $s=2$. Then $d^2(tqp+e)+s=100\times(60+1)+2=6102$.

**Answer: 6102**

prompt: In the United Kingdom a pint is 20 fluid ounces, while in the USA a pint is 16 fluid ounces. The fluid ounce has the same volume in both countries, and there are 8 pints in a gallon. My car averages 60 miles per gallon in England. How many miles per gallon can I expect it to do in similar conditions in America?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
A UK gallon is $8\times20=160$ fl oz and a US gallon is $8\times16=128$ fl oz. The car travels $60/160$ miles per fl oz, so on a US gallon it goes $\frac{60}{160}\times128=48$ miles.

**Answer: 48 miles per gallon**

prompt: Rachel, Nicky and Shona buy a large packet of popcorn. Rachel eats $\frac14$ of the packet and passes it to Nicky, who eats $\frac15$ of the remainder before passing it to Shona who eats $\frac16$ of what is left. What fraction of the packet remains for them to pass on to Steve?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
After Rachel $\frac34$ remains; after Nicky $\frac45\times\frac34=\frac35$ remains; after Shona $\frac56\times\frac35=\frac12$ remains.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

prompt: Jane puts her hand into an opaque bag containing seven pairs of gloves. There are four red pairs and three green pairs. In each pair the left glove is different to the right glove. Jane pulls out one glove at a time. How many must she pull out to be certain of a pair?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
In the worst case Jane pulls out only left gloves (or only right gloves): there are 7 left gloves (4 red, 3 green). The 8th glove must be a right glove, and there is a left glove of the same colour among those already taken, which makes a pair. So 8 are needed (and 7 are not enough).

**Answer: 8 gloves**

prompt: Which three-digit number is not a prime, is palindromic and has the sum of its digits equal to seven?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
A palindrome $aba$ with $2a+b=7$: $a=1,b=5$ gives $151$ (prime); $a=2,b=3$ gives $232$; $a=3,b=1$ gives $313$ (prime). Only $232=2\times116$ is not prime.

**Answer: 232**

prompt: To celebrate the maths club's 150th birthday Dr Smith has ordered 168 commemorative items. To pay for this he has included, in his order, a number of items for sale. Of the order, $\frac13$ are mugs to be given free to the members and $\frac1{12}$ are ties which will be given to helpers and staff. The rest of the items will be sold. How many items were for sale?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\frac13+\frac1{12}=\frac5{12}$ of the items are given away: $\frac5{12}\times168=70$. So $168-70=98$ were for sale.

**Answer: 98**

prompt: A cuboid has a square base and is $1\frac12$ times as high as it is wide. The shortest edges are 12 cm long. What is the volume of the cuboid?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The base is $12\times12$ and the height is $1.5\times12=18$ cm. Volume $=12\times12\times18=2592$ cm$^3$.

**Answer: 2592 cm$^3$**

prompt: Mrs Christie invested £80 000 while Mr Dickens invested £60 000. They shared the profits of £23 800 in the ratio of their investments. How much profit did Mr Dickens receive?

prompt: A 10 lb turkey needs to be cooked by 19:30 and the oven takes 20 minutes to heat up to the right temperature. The cooking time is then 20 minutes per pound. What is the latest time at which the oven can be turned on?

solutions.title: Solution

prompt: Joshua averages 34 marks in nine tests. His average mark for the first five tests is 37 and in the last five his average is 32 marks. What was his score for the fifth test?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The first five tests total $185$, the last five $160$, so together they count the fifth test twice: $185+160=345$. The nine tests total $9\times34=306$. The fifth test is $345-306=39$.

**Answer: 39**

prompt: Great-granny GG takes one a day of each of two types of tablet, A and B. Tablet A is in packs of 30, tablet B in packs of 25. GG starts new packets of both on 1 July. On what date will she next start new packets of both?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
She starts new packs together after $\text{lcm}(30,25)=150$ days. Counting from 1 July: 1 Aug is $+31$, 1 Sep $+62$, 1 Oct $+92$, 1 Nov $+123$, so $+150$ is $27$ days after 1 November: 28 November.

**Answer: 28 November**

prompt: What is the product of the smallest two-digit prime number and the largest two-digit Fibonacci number?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The smallest two-digit prime is $11$; the Fibonacci numbers go $\ldots,34,55,89,144$, so the largest two-digit one is $89$. $11\times89=979$.

**Answer: 979**

prompt: Peter and Alan are sitting facing each other on opposite sides of a desk. Peter uses a calculator, and an example of how his calculator displays its answers is shown below. For one question, Peter's calculator shows the answer 2016. Alan sees a different number, since the calculator is upside-down for him. What is the difference between their two numbers?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Turned through $180^\circ$, the display reads in reverse order with each digit rotated: $6\to9$, $1\to1$, $0\to0$, $2\to2$. So 2016 appears as $9102$. The difference is $9102-2016=7086$.

**Answer: 7086**

prompt: Mike runs eight laps of the school track at 66 seconds per lap and Jane runs the eight laps in 9 minutes and 4 seconds at a steady speed. What is the difference in their average times for one lap?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Jane takes $544$ s for 8 laps, i.e. $68$ s per lap. The difference is $68-66=2$ seconds.

**Answer: 2 seconds**

prompt: Charlie bought 200 shirts at £4.50 each and increased that by 60% to calculate the selling price. He sold 101 shirts and, to sell the rest, he offered them at 3 for the price of 2. How much profit, in pence, did he make on each of the last 99 shirts?

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The selling price is $4.50\times1.6=£7.20$. At 3 for the price of 2, three shirts cost $14.40$, i.e. $£4.80$ each. Profit per shirt $=4.80-4.50=£0.30=30$ pence.

**Answer: 30 pence**
